evidence.head_tones: Pixel-sampled the head region of each figure (script under scratch dir, deleted after use). Result is a clean 2-2-2 split across exactly 3 tones: figures 1 and 4 sample ~(249,233,207), a close match to #f5ead6 (Euclidean dist ~8); figures 2 and 5 sample ~(223,177,128), a close match to #e2b78c (dist ~14); figures 3 and 6 sample ~(134,91,59), a somewhat lighter rendering of #7a4f33 (dist ~20) but clearly a third distinct darker tier shared by exactly those two figures, not a per-figure invented tone. No fourth tone present.
evidence.hair_silhouettes: Figures 1, 2, and 5 share one short side-parted silhouette; figure 3 has a curly/textured silhouette; figure 6 has a top-bun/updo; figure 4 is bald with side hair only. Treating the bald head as the instructed judgment-call carve-out (no hair, not a 'style'), that leaves 3 distinct hairstyle silhouettes among the 5 haired figures (side-part / curly / bun), at the cap.
evidence.anchor_not_uniform: The 6 figures read as a varied anonymous crowd: 3 distinct head tones, 3+1 distinct hair treatments, and different garment colours/types (button shirts, sweaters, cardigan, skirts, trousers) across the set despite sharing the crowd-rig's squat body proportion and dot-eye/simple-mouth face by design. Does not read as clones.

crowd-exemplar.notes: Borderline on hair_silhouettes: the curly and bun silhouettes each currently appear on only one figure (not literally 'repeating' within this group of 6), while the side-part style repeats 3x. I ruled pass because the instruction's 'at most three' is a cap on the catalog of distinct shapes (which holds, ≤3 among haired figures) rather than a literal ≥2-occurrences-each requirement, and a 6-person set needs some texture/gender variety that a strict 2x-per-style minimum can't accommodate. Also borderline on head_tones: the dark-brown pair renders a bit lighter (dist ~20) than the pale/tan pairs' near-exact matches (dist ~8-14), but it is consistently reproduced across both dark figures, not an invented one-off, so it still reads as the third canonical tier.
